 In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack

 Vs.
State of Odisha and Others .....

Opposite Parties

08.04.2024 Order No.
This matter is taken up by hybrid mode.
Heard Mr. K.C. Dash, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Mr. B. Mohanty, learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for the State-opposite parties.

3. The petitioner has filed this writ petition seeking to quash the order dated 25.05.2016 passed in Misc. Case No.18 of 2015 under Annexure-8, by which opposite party no.3-Collector, Angul rejected his claim for R & R benefit under Orissa Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy 2006 and further to issue direction to the opposite parties to register the allotment of homestead land of area Ac.0.10 decimal in favour of the petitioner within a stipulated period and to pay compensation of Rs.5,52,000/- to the petitioner in lieu of service as per the said Policy.

4. Mr. K.C. Dash, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner contended that the land was acquired by the Government for establishment of an Integrated Steel Plant and Power Plant at NISHA in the district of Angul by opposite party-Jindal Steel and Power Ltd., Angul and accordingly, it established the said industry.

In the year 2006, village-Basudevpur came under acquisition under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, where all total Ac.112.75 dec. land was acquired leaving balance area Ac.33.30 dec. out of which Ac.3.46 agricultural land of the petitioner's father namely, Biren Pattnaik was also acquired from Khata No.25, Plot No.216/470 of village- Basudevpur vide 4(1) notification dated 06.01.2006 and under Section 6(1) declaration notification was made on 26.10.2006.
It is contended that though acquisition was made in the year 2006, effectively the petitioner was displaced from the land in 2013 and by that time he was major.

As per the provision contained in clause-2(c) of the said Policy, for the purpose of declaring eligibility for R & R benefits the list of displaced families will be updated on the 1st of January of the year in which physical displacement is Ashish Kumar Pattnayak vs State Of Odisha And Others ..... ... on 8 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67011681/
1 scheduled to take place provided that those families who move into the project area after determination of the cutoff date will not be eligible for any benefit.

sentences.text: It is further contended that the land of the petitioner having been acquired for establishment of the aforesaid industry following Orissa Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy 2006, alternative site was provided in which he has raised construction of house for his stay, but till date he has not been extended the benefit of employment or in lieu thereof Rs.5,52,000/-.
Therefore, the petitioner has approached this Court by filing this writ petition.

5. Mr. B. Mohanty, learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for the State-opposite parties contended that the father of the petitioner, namely, Biren Pattnaik, being the General Secretary of Basudevpur Village Committee managed to include the name of the present petitioner in the Master Data Sheet of Village- Basudevpur PDF list during socio-economic survey.
While including the name of the petitioner in the PDF list, his age was indicated to be 19 years and shown to have passed 10th standard from Board of Secondary Education, Odisha.
After verification of the documents, it was ascertained that the date of birth of the petitioner was 11.10.1991 as per the High School Certificate issued by the Board of Secondary Education, Odisha.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the cut- off date, i.e., 01.01.2009 was 17 years 2 months and 20 days.

Since the petitioner was a minor as on the cut-off date, he is not entitled to get any benefit under the R&R Policy, 2006, but was treated as a member of extended family of Biren Pattnaik whose land was acquired.
The petitioner was not a recorded tenant in respect of the acquired land.

Since the compensation under the Act, 1894 was paid to the father of the petitioner and the R&R benefits was extended to the father of the petitioner and the petitioner being minor as on the cut-off date, he is not eligible and entitled to the benefits under the R&R Policy, 2006.
Therefore, the claim made by the petitioner cannot be sustained in the eye of law.

6. Considering the contentions raised by learned counsel for the parties and after going through the records, this Court finds that there is no dispute with regard to acquisition of land of the petitioner and alternative land measuring Ac.0.10 dec. has been given for resettlement in which he has raised construction of house.
But, so far as grant of R & R benefit is concerned, the petitioner has neither been given employment nor paid Rs.5,52,000/- as per the Policy.

Therefore, the observation made by the Collector in the impugned order dated 25.05.2016 in Misc. Case No.18 of 2015 stating that the petitioner is not entitled to get the benefits under the Orissa Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy 2006 cannot be sustained in the eye of law.

Consequentially, the said order dated 25.05.2016 is liable to be quashed and is hereby quashed and this Court remits the matter to the very same authority to hear the same afresh by affording opportunity of hearing to the parties.
7. With the above observation and direction, the writ petition stands disposed of.
(DR. B.R. SARANGI) JUDGE (G. SATAPATHY) JUDGE Alok Designation:
